chapters.title: The HyperText Markup Language
chapters.description: Learn how elements, tags, attributes, and document structure define a webpage.

markup-lang-intro.title: How are web pages written?
markup-lang-intro.description: Learn how to identify tags and structure an HTML document.

blocks.text: HTML gives web pages their structure. A browser reads HTML elements and turns them into headings, paragraphs, links, images, forms, lists, and other parts of a document.

Most elements are written with an opening tag, content, and a closing tag. For example,

Hello

creates a paragraph whose text content is Hello.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.body:
Course Notes

HTML describes the meaning and structure of page content.

blocks.text: An element is the complete piece of markup. Tags mark where the element begins and ends. Attributes add extra information to an opening tag, such as the destination of a link or alternate text for an image.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.body: Start the HTML course uses an href attribute to tell the browser where the link goes.

markup-lang-practice.title: Elements and Tags Practice
markup-lang-practice.description: Practice reading and writing basic HTML elements. Each problem focuses on page structure, semantics, or attributes.

problems.prompt: Which element should be used for the main heading of a page?
Write an anchor element that links to /about with the visible text About.
What is the main purpose of the alt attribute on an image?
options: To provide text for people or tools that cannot use the image
To make the image load faster
To turn the image into a link
problems.answer: To provide text for people or tools that cannot use the image

problems.prompt: Which element best represents a self-contained post, story, or entry?
Write an unordered list with one item whose text is HTML.
